- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥0.7) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly to avoid overshoot.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤0.3) or shows sharp drops, model often underestimates; adjust upward to reflect potential rebound.
- Model consistently overpredicts in early days of the 30-day horizon (e.g., 1st–5th days) — apply downward bias to first 5 forecasts.
- After a price spike (e.g., >+5% from prior peak), model often overreacts with continued steep rise — cap forecast slope after spike.
- If sentiment history shows repeated low values (e.g., 0.0–0.3) followed by a rebound, model tends to lag — forecast should be slightly ahead of true price in such cases.
- Mean reversion bias: if 3–5 consecutive forecasts are above true outcome, reduce next forecast by 1–2% to align with historical mean reversion pattern.
- Sentiment volatility >0.3 in 3 consecutive days → model overfits noise → reduce forecast variance by 10–15% to avoid overreaction.
